summary: The design fits existing renderer and Bot Framework seams, but several contracts are underspecified: renderer configuration/context, authentication, envelope trust, and upload UX. The highest risks are SSRF/private-form submission failures, duplicate submissions, and silently discarded warnings/metadata.

suggestions.title: Make Teams renderer configuration app-scoped, not module-global
suggestions.rationale: `_RENDERERS` is a process-global registry seeded with `setdefault`, while `setup_form_api` can create multiple applications with different tenants or public URLs. Registering one environment-derived `TeamsFormRenderer` makes configuration order-dependent and difficult to test. Inject the renderer or its public URL through `setup_form_api`/app state, and define the unset behavior explicitly.

suggestions.title: Pass render context explicitly to action builders
suggestions.rationale: `_build_form_actions` and `_build_wizard_actions` receive only labels and flags, so a subclass cannot derive `form_uid`, tenant, or version without mutable renderer state or reimplementing `render`. Add an explicit optional context argument, or override the complete render method, while keeping the default renderer’s serialized output unchanged. Only the terminal wizard submit should receive a forwarding envelope; Back/Next/Cancel must retain dialog semantics.

suggestions.title: Never trust submit_url from activity.value
suggestions.rationale: The wrapper will receive a user-controlled Adaptive Card payload, and the proposed branch would POST an attacker-selected absolute URL if it trusts `_formdesigner.submit_url`. This creates an SSRF primitive. Validate a typed envelope, derive the destination from trusted configuration and the declared tenant/form UID, or verify a signature; also disable redirects and enforce an allowlist before making the request.

suggestions.title: Resolve private-form authentication before implementation
suggestions.rationale: The existing `/data` route is wrapped with `tenant="public"` middleware and then calls `enforce_membership_unless_public`; a Bot Framework POST without navigator-auth session credentials will fail for private forms. The envelope’s tenant field does not grant access. Restrict v1 to public forms or define a service credential/token propagation contract and test both 401/403 and successful public submission.

suggestions.title: Avoid duplicating value coercion in the Teams wrapper
suggestions.rationale: `FormValidator._coerce_value` already converts numeric strings, `"true"`/`"false"`, and comma-separated multi-select values before validation. A second Teams-side type map will drift from the canonical validator and cannot handle newer field types consistently. Prefer forwarding raw card values and relying on `/data`, or extract a shared pure coercion contract if the bot must normalize first.

suggestions.title: Strip an explicit control-key set, not every underscore key
suggestions.rationale: The current dialog merge helper drops all keys beginning with `_`, but `FormField.field_id` has no underscore prohibition. The proposed wrapper behavior would therefore lose legitimate answers such as `_department`. Define reserved control keys (`_action`, `_formdesigner`, and any command keys) and preserve all other field IDs, with a regression test.

suggestions.title: Expose or deliberately define the warning/metadata transport
suggestions.rationale: `handle_render` currently returns only `rendered.content`; it discards `RenderedForm.warnings` and `metadata`. Consequently the proposed upload `RenderWarning` and Teams envelope metadata are visible only to direct Python callers, not to `GET …/render/teams` clients. Decide whether the HTTP contract adds warning/metadata headers or an opt-in response envelope, and test the chosen behavior.

suggestions.title: Use the existing upload API as the integration target, not an unspecified upload-page template
suggestions.rationale: The repository already exposes authenticated multipart endpoints at `/fields/{field_uid}/file-upload` and `/fields/{field_uid}/upload`, but no web upload page is established by the cited routes. An `Action.OpenUrl` cannot perform the required multipart POST by itself. Require a configured, real browser upload page with a return protocol, or render a clear unsupported-upload instruction when none exists; test that every upload field has a usable destination.

suggestions.title: Add replay protection or idempotency
suggestions.rationale: The envelope contains form identity and version but no submission correlation or idempotency key. Teams retries, duplicate clicks, and Bot Framework redelivery can invoke `/data` multiple times, and the handler persists each successful submission. Add a signed nonce/idempotency key with server-side deduplication, or document duplicate persistence as accepted behavior and test retries.

suggestions.title: Use one reusable bounded aiohttp submit client with lifecycle ownership
suggestions.rationale: The wrapper currently has no outbound FormDesigner client or session lifecycle. Creating a `ClientSession` per card leaks resources under load, while an unbounded request can stall the Bot Framework turn. Follow the repository’s reusable-session pattern, attach timeout/response-size limits, close it through application cleanup, and map network failures to a deterministic card response.

suggestions.title: Add exact default-card compatibility and route-level contract tests
suggestions.rationale: Current Adaptive Card tests mostly assert non-null output and limited warning presence; they do not prove the required byte-identical `adaptive` contract. Add a canonical serialized golden fixture for the default renderer, a `teams` registration/503-unset test, envelope/version/metadata assertions, nested upload-warning coverage, and a wrapper test proving malformed envelopes and all non-terminal wizard actions do not fall through to dialog continuation.

suggestions.title: Define version and tenant identity precisely in the envelope
suggestions.rationale: `FormSchema.version` and `published_version` are strings, while the proposed `form_version` is shown as an integer; additionally, the render route uses the URL-declared tenant while the renderer receives only the form object. Specify whether the envelope carries the published string version or draft version, pass the validated route tenant into rendering, and reject mismatches at submission time rather than treating these fields as informational.
